label: Model forecast
method: CDIP MOP nearshore wave model (ECMWF and WW3 forced, blended and bias-corrected at the buoys), then a random-wave shoaling and breaking model (Battjes–Janssen) from the model's 10 m point to the beach, using each swell's own period and direction. Wind: Open-Meteo (NOAA HRRR/GFS). Tide: NOAA La Jolla 9410230.
credits: CDIP / Scripps Institution of Oceanography, funded by USACE and California State Parks; MOP model: O'Reilly et al. (2016), Coastal Engineering 116
Surf Zone Forecast: National Weather Service San Diego

verification.what: Wave height (Hs) at the CDIP buoys, MOP blend vs buoy observations
verification.testPeriod: 2025-04-01 to 2026-11-26 (held out; never used for tuning)
beats: plain shoaling without island sheltering (RMSE ~1 m)
verification.notVerified: Face height and rating: no surf observations yet. Treat them as model estimates.
verification.scale: On small days our heights run about 20% above NWS surf forecasts; the Scripps Pier wave sensor supports ours.
verification.observed: Big days: 56 lifeguard and official high-surf reports (NWS storm reports, 2016–2026) matched our heights (median ratio 0.99; we reached at least 80% of the reported size on 93%). Small days: our heights track the Scripps Pier wave sensor (CDIP 073) closely over 1,538 small mornings (rank correlation 0.94). Small-day face heights are not yet checked against people's observations.
verification.leadNote: Scores are short-lead. Skill by forecast day is being collected.
